question: Which coupling tests does this candidate actually satisfy against the anchor?
context: §3 The test is coupling, not similarity. Two issues belong in one cycle when solving them apart would mean doing the same work twice or would invalidate the other's measurements: they name the same surface (one panel, one screen, one control); they are owned by the same layout function, so one fix moves the other's numbers; proving one requires a validator that would also prove the other; one's fix re-pins the same validators the other would; one is Matt's own report of what an audit-derived issue describes (his wording wins, and implementing the audit's version alone leaves his issue open against the same surface).
§3 Two issues that merely sound alike, or share a subsystem without sharing geometry or a call path, are not a batch. Bundling those makes a cycle bigger and proves nothing extra.

§3 The sweep is the bottleneck. The gate is 72-90 minutes and the flock serialises it machine-wide. So coupled items MUST batch, and independent items on disjoint surfaces SHOULD. The limit is attribution, not size: batch as many items as you can attribute a red to from the failing validator alone. Where you cannot predict attribution, keep the batch smaller.

§3 Prefer items that share a FIXTURE, not merely a gate. When two candidates share a fixture, each one's pin becomes a control for the other's change at no cost. When they merely share a gate, all you save is wall clock.

§1a How much to put in one gate: a red gate with N commits has N suspects. Batch when the items are independent and each is individually proven; keep a behaviour change separate from a large mechanical move when you can.

§3 Recorded cases: #132 (the HUD's two chrome bands, from a design audit) was the same two bands as #182 and #183, Matt's own reports - implementing the audit alone would have shipped less than he asked for and left both his issues open. #129 could not be finished without #186: the WORK screen's resource column was anchored to the comms panel's live bottom edge, so a mode-dependent panel height moved it.
constraints: The anchor is fixed and is not a candidate. Every answer is about joining THIS anchor's cycle.
Similarity is not coupling. Sharing a subsystem without sharing geometry or a call path is not coupling.
Answer 'no' when the only thing gained would be a bigger cycle.
Answer 'none' alone when nothing fires. Never pair 'none' with another option.

categories.same-surface: names the same panel, screen or control
categories.same-layout-function: owned by the same layout function, so one fix moves the other's numbers
categories.shared-validator: proving one requires a validator that would also prove the other
categories.repins-same-validators: one's fix re-pins the same validators the other would
categories.matts-own-report: one is Matt's own report of what an audit-derived issue describes
categories.shared-fixture: both drive the same test fixture, so each pin controls the other
